entities.summary: Branicki Palace is a historical edifice in Białystok, Poland. It was developed on the site of an earlier building in the first half of the 18th century by Jan Klemens Branicki, a wealthy Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth hetman, into a residence suitable for a man whose ambition was to become king of Poland. The palace complex with gardens, pavilions, sculptures, outbuildings and other structures and the city with churches, city hall and monastery, all built almost at the same time according to French models was the reason why the city was known in the 18th century as Versailles de la Pologne and subsequently Versailles de la Podlachie.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Branicki Palace played a significant role in shaping the Baroque architectural style in Eastern Europe, influencing the development of subsequent royal residences and city planning. Its impact can be seen in the numerous palaces built in Poland during the 18th century.
